$comment: Which external document each reference in IAES_SPEC.md means, and whether it can be consulted. Normative for what IAES may cite: a claim about a document nobody can open is a claim nobody can check. It says nothing about whether the document supports what IAES attributes to it -- that is a separate question, and this file deliberately does not answer it.

vocabulary.id: The identity this registry answers about. A document, not a family: an edition where one is known, because clause numbering differs between editions and translations.

availability.public: Published without charge by its publisher. Anyone can consult the same text.
availability.available: Not public, and a copy is held. Requires access_basis and, where the copy is a specific edition, that edition and language.
availability.unavailable: Not public and no copy held. A claim about it cannot be checked without buying it.
availability.unresolved: The citation does not identify a document, so availability cannot be asked. Requires resolution before it can be answered.

vocabulary.access_basis: How the copy was obtained. steward_copy means the editor holds a purchased copy.

references.note: The copy held is the 2024 Spanish edition. A clause cited from it must name that edition and language: numbering can differ between translations and editions, and 'ISO 55000' alone is not an interchangeable object.
The code list is widely mirrored; the standard document is not held. Recorded as unavailable rather than assumed, because 'everybody knows it' is how unverifiable attributions get made.

Cited as a series, so it names no document and availability cannot be answered. Measured: the citations cover at least two different subjects -- health status levels and a six-block processing model -- which cannot both be one part. Of the series only 13374-4:2015 (en) is held; 13374-2, which Appendix C depends on, is not. Resolving each citation to a part is editorial work; rfc/IAES-RFC-002.md proposes withdrawing the attributions instead.

held_but_not_cited.$comment: Documents the editor holds that this specification does not cite. Recorded so that 'we have it' is never confused with 'we use it', and so a future citation knows an edition is already available.
